title: Zbtb11 loss represses a mitochondrial, nucleolar, endomembrane, and glycan program in vulnerable subcortical neurons
exact_observed_result: Zbtb11 perturbation produced 48 FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 17 in 191 MB P MY GABA, and 16 in 155 MB Glut. The recurrent core was down-regulated and included Rbm28, Taf1b, Stx16, Pigq, Man2c1, Gtpbp3, Acsf3, Ndufc2, Ndufaf1, and Ttc4, with 151 TH examples such as Rbm28 logFC -1.460 FDR 3.57e-16 and Acsf3 logFC -1.146 FDR 7.68e-09.
biological_interpretation: Zbtb11 loss selectively suppresses a mixed mitochondrial, RNA polymerase I/nucleolar, endomembrane, GPI-biosynthesis, and glycan-catabolic abundance program, matching known ZBTB11 mitochondrial and neurodevelopmental disease biology but showing that the response is not shared by arbitrary ZBTB-family perturbations.
caveats: FDR gene counts correlated with perturbed-cell counts across cell types, and ZBTB-family comparator tests do not include known GABP/NRF-2 partners.

prior_expectation.summary: ZBTB11 cooperates with NRF-2/GABP to activate nuclear mitochondrial genes and biallelic ZBTB11 variants cause intellectual disability with biochemical ACSF3 effects, supporting the mitochondrial branch of the Perturb-seq response.
